series.name: KMC-GM Series

source.note: All values transcribed from the printed catalogue. Nothing in this file is AI-estimated.

tool_magazine.note: Total weight of full blade is less than 160 kg

series.model_code_rule: First digit = X travel in metres (3→3000 … 6→6000); '25' = distance between columns 2500 mm. Series-constant specs identical across models; only X travel, table length, rapids, floor space and weight vary.

features.title: Box-in-Box Design
features.copy: Thermal symmetry construction with a fully integrated crossbeam, improving rigidity by 32%.

features.title: Z-Axis Dual Motor Drive
features.copy: High-speed movement with high precision and fast dynamic response without oil-pressure hysteresis — no high-pressure hydraulic cylinder. Suitable for high-precision cutting.

features.title: THK Linear Guideways & Ballscrews
features.copy: THK made-in-Japan linear guideways and ballscrews ensure high quality and precision.

features.title: Three-Axes Cooling System
features.copy: Inner-cooled ballscrews, head-and-tail cooling and a motor board with cooling circuit give optimal control over thermal growth on all three axes. Patented unique design M634822.

features.title: KESSLER 2-Axis Head
features.copy: Five-axis capability through a KESSLER two-axis milling head with HSK-A100 interface and standard coolant-through-spindle.

features.title: Chain-Type Tool Magazine
features.copy: Standard 32-tool chain magazine, HSK-A100 shank, with a tool-changing arm for greater stability and longevity.

features.title: Self-Milling Working Table
features.copy: Working table finish-machined by the machine itself.

specs.spindle_speed_rpm: 12000–30000 (KESSLER head product range as printed; machine specification 15000 rpm)

specs.design: Thermal symmetry construction, fully integrated crossbeam

specs.drive: Dual motor, without high-pressure hydraulic cylinder

flagship_pilot.rationale: The catalogue's GM floor-space drawing corresponds to the 325GM footprint (9300 mm length); drawings + full spec column verified in hand. GM models differ only in X-length — the 425/525/625GM 3D variants derive from the 325GM model by stretching X-direction segments (base, table, enclosure), so one build yields four machines.
